messages:
alan: FYI folks — next Tuesday 09:00 PT we're enabling org-wide SSO enforcement + SCIM group sync via our new Okta GitHub app. This will phase out legacy personal access tokens (PATs) used for repo automation unless they're migrated to app tokens or OIDC. :warning:

priya: Quick Q: will this break service accounts that use PATs right away?

alan: Short answer: yes for any PATs created after the enforcement cutoff. For existing PATs we9ll put them in a grace window (30 days) and emit audit warnings. We strongly recommend migrating to app auth or OIDC short-lived tokens.

emily: Migration steps for infra/service accounts?

alan: Two paths:
1) CI/runner jobs: switch to GitHub Actions OIDC or the new org app tokens (we9ll provide a terraform module).
2) Bots/long-running services: create an 'app principal' in Okta and bind via SCIM to the GitHub org membership role. Docs link below has examples.

marc: Will group membership be authored in Okta only?

alan: Yes — Okta is the source of truth for groups. We9ll sync: engineering, infra-admins, security-oncall, partners. Any manual GH team changes will be overwritten. Please review your mapped groups.

priya: What about integrations like Dependabot, Snyk, and release tooling?

alan: Dependabot and GH Apps that already use app auth are unaffected. For vendors using PATs we9ll contact vendor admins and open tickets to migrate. If you manage an integration that needs help, tag @it-helpdesk and include the repo list.

emily: Is 2FA being enforced as part of this?

alan: Yes — 2FA and device trust will be required for interactive logins. Service principals using app auth are exempted. We9ll surface non-compliant accounts in a weekly report starting today.

security-bot: Scheduled check: org-ssopolicy-audit run created. Will DM owners of noncompliant accounts every 24h for 30 days.

priya: Any dev-facing commands to test local setup?

alan: Use GitHub CLI + browser auth or SSH keys (still supported but team-owned deploy keys will be removed). Example for CLI login:

```bash
# login via web flow
gh auth login --web
# verify PAT presence (should be empty normally)
gh auth status
```

marc: How will this affect self-hosted runners that use repo-scoped tokens?

alan: Runners should use the runner service token provisioned by the org app. If you run self-hosted pools, update your runner config to reference the new token endpoint: `https://oidc.internal.redwood/v1/runner/token`. Runners will fetch a short-lived token at boot and auto-refresh.

emily: Timeline?

alan: Rollout schedule:
- Today: announcement and docs publish (done)
- 7 days: start SCIM sync dry-run (no changes, just logs)
- 14 days: warn noncompliant accounts via audit emails
- 30 days: enable enforcement (automated removal of legacy PAT access)

priya: Rollback plan if there's a big integration failure?

alan: Short rollback: pause enforcement flag in Okta-GH app (instant), re-enable PAT acceptance for affected repos, and run restoration script that re-adds service tokens. We'll also maintain an audit snapshot so we can restore removed deploy keys.

it-helpdesk: If you need manual migration assistance, file ticket with label `ssomigration` and include repo names + integration owners. SLA: 48 hours for critical infra repos.

marc: Who is on-call during the flip?

alan: @emily and @tina will be on-call the day enforcement is enabled. Contact via pager or this channel.

emily: Added a short checklist for teams:
- Confirm users in Okta for your GH teams
- Replace PATs in CI with OIDC/app tokens
- Update self-hosted runner config to new token endpoint
- Check vendor integrations and open tickets if they use PATs

alan: Docs: https://intranet.redwood.com/security/sso-scim-migration (includes terraform module, runner example, and rollback scripts). Please read before EOD Friday.

tina: Reminder: do not delete old deploy keys until after the 30-day grace period. We keep a backup snapshot that we can reapply.

priya: Thanks — I'll start auditing our repos and open tickets for the few services that still rely on PATs.

alan: Thanks team. We'll post a short post-mortem and notes after enforcement completes. :lock:
